question: What is the UK National Living Wage hourly rate for workers aged 21 and over from April 2026?
answer:
The UK National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026, up £0.50 (4.1 per cent) from £12.21 [2][3][4]. The regulations setting this rate extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland [8]. The National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Regulations 2026 amend regulation 4 of the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015, replacing £12.21 with £12.71, and extend to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland [8]. Workers aged 21 or over who are not in the first year of an apprenticeship are legally entitled to at least this rate [4].

This is general legal information based on UK sources, and rules differ in other jurisdictions. For a specific pay situation, a licensed lawyer or Acas can advise, and the government's guidance says suspected underpayment can be reported to HMRC [4].

keyPoints.text: The National Living Wage for workers aged 21 and over is £12.71 per hour from 1 April 2026.
This is a 4.1 per cent increase, or £0.50 per hour, on the previous rate of £12.21.
The increase took effect on 1 April 2026 following Low Pay Commission recommendations accepted by the Government.
The regulations amending the rate from £12.21 to £12.71 came into force on 1 April 2026.
